# Chapter Three: In The Name Of The Father

Sam was not happy, not happy at all his eminence was specific about choosing Victor, He wouldn’t tell him why. But Same knew what they were hunting and he definitely didn’t want his friend to be brought into the middle of this. The Bishop knew something that he was keeping to himself. This kill made no sense, it wasn’t like all the others this was too high profile, too easy to find dammit and that was the problem. They had gotten the call from there contact at the DOJ and within a few calls they had their Justice escorts and were on their way.

He had not been with the order long, only about a year but the things he had seen would be enough to drive any sane man mad. They had hunted 2 since he had been brought into the fold. Only he, the bishop and three others of the order knew what they did and more importantly what they hunted. They currently had 6 hunters at their disposal of which Edgar was the best. They were lucky he was in Virginia tracking a pack that had come across from Ohio when this happened. He had high tailed it here within two hours and was on scene. Sam thought Edgar was as perplexed as the rest of them, not once had a body been left so blatantly for them to find. It was like they were baiting them, or someone. Sam knew they were searching for something. The family killed in San Bernardino last year, the Old man and his grandson in Ohio. But this was a nobody, a runner with no connection or family name. But the fact that it had been left here, of all places for anyone to find, they had to know hunters would be crawling all over the area within a day and that no rock would be left unturned. Why would they risk this, what would it gain them Too many questions with no answers and Sam didn’t like it. The Bishop was also stonewalling him. Making him choose his childhood friend as the liaison he didn’t even know they knew each other until he handed Sam the folder and he said something, the small smile on the face of the Bishop was odd. It was like a piece had fit together and Sam just didn’t see it.

Edgar knew something was up. He could see him and his eminence talking in hushed tones but Edgar clearly was upset. He would have to find out why later, since the Bishop wouldn’t tell him maybe Edgar would. Same scanned the trees and held the silver cross he kept in his pocket tightly. They could be watching, that would be like them wouldn’t it, waiting to see who showed up, see if they could get the scent of the hunter. Sam watched Vic as he looked over the scene, he didn’t want Vic in this, not with Jessica and the kids at home. If they were watching what would happen if they marked him thinking he was a hunter. Sam would never forgive himself if anything happened to his friend or the family, after his parents had died the kids and Jessica were all he had.

He had lost his way, Victor was a good catholic, like himself they loved the church, worked it every Sunday helping father Duncan with anything they could, hell they were altar boys together. But after the car accident Vic had stopped going to church, he had stopped everything It wasn’t until years later when he had heard his friend had gotten married that he had hope that he might return to a normal life. Sam said a quick prayer for his friend.

“Father Lawrence, could I have a word with you, in private” called Bishop Taylor. Breaking Sam out of his thoughts. He turned to look at the bishop and could see the serious set in his face “Of course your eminence” He turned back to where Vic was examining a piece of the corpse “Vic, ill be right back, if you have any questions please ask Edgar, and again please don’t touch anything until the crime lab has a chance to go through it” Vic waved at him and Sam stepped over to the Bishop. “Walk with me father, please” the bishop said extending his hand up the canal walk, “Of course sir” he started up the dirt path with the Bishop next to him. Sam strolled along the path for a few minutes appreciating the trees but his mind a turmoil of questions and worries, once they were far enough from the others Same stood looking at the trees “Sir, I have issues with this, it makes no sense for them to leave a body like this, are we sure it was them?” Sam asked hopeful. “The bishop just stared out over the Woodline, “Edgar used the cross, it was them and they were here as recently as within an hour of the body being found so they stayed long enough to ensure that it happened.

Sam’s hope deflated like a balloon. “Why would they leave a body in a such a public display sir, this makes no sense I, they would have to know we would have hunters combing this area as soon as it was found. There is no way they would take that risk, it’s too much even for them.” Sam said his frustration showing. And sir, I don’t mean to question your decisions but I have to ask” The Bishop smiled and nodded his head “Why Victor Handy” he said smiling. Sam let out a sigh, “Yes sir, why him I would prefer to keep him as far from this as possible, the man has suffered too much loss and he is a friend”

The Bishop nodded, “I understand son, I truly do but god works in mysterious ways, have you noticed the patterns we have been tracking for the last year and the data that goes back even further. They are nomadic by nature, isolated packs stick to their own territory and only moved when threatened, but these past 5 years they have been moving steadily from one end of the country to the other, haven’t you wondered why my boy” The Bishop asked. “Look at the pattern and tell me what it suggests to you” Sam shook his head, another lesson, always a lesson with Bishop Taylor, the man was a good teacher, but even after a while lessons could get tiresome, but Same knew better then to try and get to the point when he was in one of his moods. “It’s like they are being directed, told where to go and when to move. Its like they are looking for something” The Bishop nodded pleased with the answer.

“And who could direct not one but at least 12 separate packs at once” He asked again, leading Sam with another question that only had one answer “A prince, only a prince could have that power over that many packs, But why Sir, what could they be looking for, we have had them on the run for at least 50 years and they are all but extinct in Europa, Asia and Italy, the most activity we have seen as been in the states in the last century, but not one of our analysts or scribes can tell us why that would be, would they not stick to prime hunting ground like Brazil or Canada where there is more wooded area and less likely that they would be caught” Sam asked the question that had been weighing on him since he had started looking at the data a year ago.

“Yes, that would be the logical choice, and we have seen some activity in those areas but not like we should, it seems there is a good concentration here in the states and they are looking for something or someone.” This kill, this display tells me they thing they are close, they are hunters, predators and what do predators do when they feel there quarry is close? “The Bishop asked. Sam thought through the lessons he had been taught about the creatures “They flush them out, but how does that have anything to do with this” He couldn’t seem to put the two together. Bishop Taylor smiled at his young protégé, he liked Sam, he was a good honest priest who loved the church, in fact it had been Taylor who had recommended he be approached for the order, after watching his career as a priest he truly felt that this young man would be the future of the order and possibly even take his place once day.

“Because my dear boy, they feel they have found what they are looking for, or at least close so they are trying to flush them out.” Sam thought on that for a moment, what could they hope to attack with this type of kill, or whom. He couldn’t see the logic in it. “I’m sorry sir, I just can’t see it” The bishop nodded, I know son, neither do I yet, all I have is hunches right now, but we will have to see how this plays out. In the meantime, I want you to stay very close to our friend Victor, I am not sure yet but something tells me he has a part to play in all this” he said looking back over at the park policemen. “Sir, can I ask a question, I don’t want to question your methods, but something has been bothering me” The bishop looked at the younger priest. “Ask away my boy” Sam gathered his thoughts and looked at the steel haired bishop “What calls did you make prior to choosing Victor, it seems that whatever was said resolved your decision, and if I am to watch him I would like to know what you suspect sir”. The Bishop thought for a moment and then looked Sam in the eye. “That is not important as of yet, but know if my hunch plays out your friend could be in grave danger, so stay close to him, if my hunch doesn’t then it will just be a chance for you to catch up with an old friend” The Bishop smiled, “Let’s get you two out and searching the surrounding area, maybe our friends got careless and left something for us” He stepped away from Sam and began to walk back towards the crime scene, his way of telling Sam the conversation was over.

Vic had noticed the two priests heading off, this was just getting better and better, he wasn’t sure what was going on but this wasn’t some simple investigation, these guys knew something about this, and the fact the Justice guys seemed to take a second fiddle to the priests was rather telling, it seems they were just here for window dressing. He had never heard of anything like this before. “Feeling a little over your head on this one my friend” ask the baritone voice of Edgar from behind him. Vic turned around to see the smiling man kneeling close by examining a bone “Just a bit, hell the fact is I feel like I am riding the titanic all the way down right about now” He said smiling to the man, Vic liked him, he had a good sense about people and Edgar seemed like an okay guy. “What do you make of all this, I mean this is like the body was put on some kind of grotesque display, whatever or whoever did this had to know it would be found, and the fact that there is so much left, it looks like a statement, I mean I am no profiler but damn” Vic extended his hands up and down the shore. Edgar nodded “I agree” he stood up and walked over to Vic, Vic noticed he was holding something in his hand, “Hey Edgar what is that” he said pointing to the object. Edgar held it out to him and Vic took it and examined it, it was a metal cross with an odd diagram in the center “It feels warm, I mean really warm” he said looking at the man. Edgar actually looked surprised, it was the first emotion aside from that affable smile he had seen on the man’s face “truly, you feel the warmth of it?” he asked not able to hide the surprise in his voice. “Yeah, are you running a fever or is it something to do with the metal, like two metals that react, something like that? “Vic asked. Edgar took the cross back and put it in his pocket. “Yeah something like that” he said looking over his shoulder at the priests. Since the priests weren’t in earshot Vic figured it was as good a time as any to try and get a little information on the situation “So Edgar, what the hell is this about, I mean I know this isn’t an animal attack, I’ve done enough hunting in my youth to know what that looks like, but some of these marks are not done by a human hand, what am I missing here man” Edgar turned and looked at him, his steel blue eyes searching Vic’s “That’s very astute for someone who has never worked a murder scene my friend, I can’t really talk about it, but what did this, is not something you want to ever come up against” he said and the look in his eyes told Vic volumes, like first he was right he really didn’t and second that this man had knowledge, intimate knowledge of what did this, that sent a shiver up Vic’s back. What the hell had he gotten into.

Sam returned with the bishop moments later and called Vic over. “So the Bishop wishes us to comb the area to see if we can find anything that might have been missed” Vic looked at him like he had two heads “You mean that the legion of police and crime people might have overlooked?” Sam nodded Okay Vic thought, at least it would give him a chance to see what could find out, his day had been turned upside down since arriving this morning. God had it only been two hours since he had arrived “Alright Sammy, let’s go combing” he said using his friend’s childhood name.
